moc.chu: On 13 March 1781 while making observations he made note of a new object in the constellation of Gemini.
Herschel originally thought it was a comet or a stellar disc, which he believed he might actually resolve.
Its nearly circular orbit suggested that it was a planet rather than a comet.
In a March 1782 treatise, Johann Elert Bode proposed Uranus, the Latinised version of the Greek god of the sky, Ouranos.
